routes.label: Reflect to create an inscribed angle

question:
In this figure the radius of the circle is equal to the altitude of the equilateral triangle \(ABC.\) The circle is made to roll along the side \(AB,\) remaining tangent to it at a variable point \(T\) and intersecting lines \(AC\) and \(BC\) in variable points \(M\) and \(N,\) respectively. Let \(n\) be the number of degrees in arc \(MTN.\) Then \(n,\) for all permissible positions of the circle:

[Figure 1](figures/1964_AMC_12_Q36_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
[Figure 1](figures/1964_AMC_12_Q36_question_fig1.svg)

Use the intersections \(M\) on \(CA\) and \(N\) on \(CB\) labeled in the figure. Let \(O\) be the circle's center and \(h\) the triangle's altitude. The radius \(OT\) is perpendicular to the tangent \(AB\), and \(OT=h\). Thus \(O\) and \(C\) have the same height above \(AB\). Let \(\ell\) be the line through them parallel to \(AB\); if \(O=C\), take the parallel through that common point.

Reflection across \(\ell\) preserves the circle because \(\ell\) passes through its center. It also sends line \(AC\) to line \(BC\): these lines pass through \(C\) and make equal \(60^\circ\) angles with the base on opposite slopes.

Reflect \(M\) across \(\ell\), calling its image \(X\). Then \(X\) lies on both the circle and line \(BC\), and \(MX\) is perpendicular to \(AB\). Since \(X\) is above \(\ell\) and \(N\) is below it, ray \(XN\) runs down line \(BC\). Therefore
\[
\angle MXN=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ.
\]
To identify the intercepted arc, notice that \(C\) lies between \(X\) and \(N\), so it is inside the circle. For interior contact points \(T\), the rays \(CM,CT,CN\) occur in that order within the triangle's angle at \(C\). Their circle intersections consequently occur in the order \(M,T,N\) on the arc avoiding \(X\). Thus the inscribed angle \(MXN\) intercepts precisely arc \(MTN\), and
\[
n=2\angle MXN=60^\circ.
\]
If endpoint contact is included, \(T=A\) gives \(M=T\), and \(T=B\) gives \(N=T\). The same inscribed angle still determines the corresponding lower arc, whose measure is \(60^\circ\). Hence \(n\) remains constant at \(\boxed{60^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
